_baseline_note: R-MFDN T cell (BERT-base-uncased 110M fine-tuned, mask-weighted mean pool), P2 fold f0, reference-free (i3), visibility-aligned (single visible bit llm_textgen, nkeep=1 so test.mAP == llm AP); BSC $S/runs4f/f0/T_base (5.9 min train, best_val 62.60). Test: ACC 63.45 / AUC 66.86 / mAP 91.60. Ladder so far on this fold: E004 order-blind bag 2.1M -> llm AP 56.81; E005 bag + 2-layer transformer 2.3M -> 75.74.

factor._note: absent = BERT-base (paper encoder). bertmini = the same TextEncoder (mask-weighted mean pool + Linear 256->512) over prajjwal1/bert-mini (4 layers x 256 hidden, 4 heads, FFN 1024; 11,170,560 encoder params, 11.30M with projection; MLM-pretrained, uncased WordPiece vocab byte-identical to bert-base-uncased so the tokenizer is unchanged), fine-tuned end to end at the same LR. Checkpoint path lives in the environment key bert_mini_model (BSC $S/env/models/bert-mini, pytorch_model.bin md5 83cb6c1bb924adb5c34d7110dfbb840d, from HF hub 2026-10-01).

hypothesis: Language pretraining, not width or depth, closes the remaining gap on the llm_textgen bit: a pretrained 11M BERT-mini fine-tuned like BERT-base reaches f0 test llm AP >= 90.0 (BERT-base 91.60; from-scratch 2-layer transformer 75.74), while staying inside C0's 14-17M total budget; AUC within +-2 of 66.86.
_success_note: test.mAP is exactly llm_textgen AP here (nkeep=1). make_run_report's verdict is strict-sign against BERT-base; the pre-registered gate is watched.llm_textgen >= 90.0 (equivalence). 75.74-90 would mean pretraining helps but capacity also matters -> next rung BERT-small (29M) or distillation from BERT-base.
